newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi's Ibn Sina signs $215 mln loan with banks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Ibn Sina signs $215 mln loan with banks.

text.p: Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) subsidiary Ibn Sina has signed an 806 million riyal ($215 million) syndicated loan with seven local and regional banks, a Saudi banker said.
Ibn Sina, which is also called the National Methanol Co, is 50 percent owned by SABIC. U.S. firms Pan Energy and Hoechst-Celanese each hold 25 percent.

The 8-1/2 year loan is led by Saudi American Bank (SAMBA), which is 30 percent owned by Citibank. The other participating banks are Saudi British Bank, Gulf International Bank, Al-Bank Al-Saudi Al-Fransi, Saudi Investment Bank, Bank al-Jazira and Arab National Bank.
Bankers declined to give the margin over LIBOR.
The loan was signed in Riyadh on Tuesday by Ibn Sina Chairman Mohammad al-Musallam and SAMBA head of syndication, Abdulaziz al-Barakat.
Ibn Sina, based in Jubail, produces chemical-grade methanol and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE).
